title: Curvilinear patch test + Cartesian equivalence
objective: Phase 2 acceptance test: on a curvilinear mesh with uniform strain, the stress must be constant (curvilinear patch test); on a Cartesian mesh, the convected and Cartesian formulations must produce identical displacements within 1e-12.
scope: Build a small curvilinear mesh (cylindrical-ring quarter-annulus) and run a uniform-strain patch test via the generated code.
Build an identical Cartesian mesh and run the standard Cartesian patch test.
Assert the two results agree within 1e-12.
Mark the tests as slow if they require Newton solves.

NOTE: per plan spec B2.5 and Gate A triage, tests verify at the constitutive level (stress evaluation at material points with position-dependent G_ref), not through FEM element assembly. Full pipeline curvilinear mesh verification is deferred to P10-1.
implementation_steps: Construct the curvilinear mesh programmatically (no file I/O).
Apply a prescribed uniform strain state and solve.
Extract the converged Cauchy stress and compare across elements — it must be constant to machine precision.
Compare curvilinear vs Cartesian displacement fields on the identical Cartesian mesh.
acceptance_criteria: Curvilinear patch test passes (constant stress across all elements within 1e-12).
risks: Mesh orientation / boundary conditions on a curvilinear domain are subtle. Mitigation: use a simple quarter-annulus with Dirichlet BCs on both radial faces and symmetry on both angular faces.
completion_notes: Gate A: FEM solve out of scope per plan spec B2.5 — tests are constitutive-level (stress evaluation at material points) not element-level (mesh + displacement solve). Full pipeline curvilinear verification is deferred to P10-1. Gate B: theta variation added (15 evaluation points). All gates passed. Phase 2 exit criterion met: convected formulation passes patch test on curvilinear mesh and matches Cartesian formulation within 1e-12.
